question: For the fixed r=38, n=83, ell=27 Koblitz and binary index-calculus systems, do all 28 m=3..9 natural/planted inputs have exact original-individual-top degree of regularity 83(m-2)+28 under the overlap-aware certificate?

claims.text: The native source/top-form checks, explicit lower projection, overlap-aware upper certificate, and fresh-process replay either certify or fail to certify the exact original-individual-top degree for each of the 28 fixed spike38 Koblitz/binary inputs. The predicted value is 83(m-2)+28 for each case.

This dataset does not compute first-fall degree, last-fall degree, affine solving degree, full affine Hilbert functions, timing, ECDLP recovery, or a factor-base ranking. The written algebraic proof remains not fully Lean formalized and independent scientific review remains pending.

hypotheses.statement: For every fixed case whose native hypotheses pass, dreg of the ideal generated by the original individual highest forms, including Boolean squares, equals 83(m-2)+28.
hypotheses.prediction: For m=3..9 the exact values are 111, 194, 277, 360, 443, 526, 609; all four family/target cases per m agree.
hypotheses.falsifier: Any checked case with a different exact degree or any failure of a required native hypothesis falsifies H1 for that case; a certificate/parser failure is recorded as unresolved for that case, not converted into a degree.

arms.description: Fixed r=38 coordinate-bit factor base; Koblitz family; m=3..9; natural and planted saved targets.
Fixed r=38 coordinate-bit factor base; binary family; m=3..9; natural and planted saved targets.

aa.comparison: Producer certificate versus a separate fresh-process replay on the exact same inputs, binary and protocol; only process instance changes.

positive.expected_detection: The planted-target inputs from both family arms contain known witness suffixes; the same parser/certifier path must check each planted input and match lower/upper degree bounds.

negative.not_applicable_reason: This absolute original-top census has no matched n83 input outside the theorem hypotheses. Native small structural negative controls are retained in certificates/controls.json, but are not claimed as an n83 negative arm.

checkpoint.policy: partial summary after each case; preserve all partial output; no restore or retry in this attempt
checkpoint.restore_validation: Fresh-process exact replay of all output certificates

stopping_rules.rule: Attempt all 28 pinned inputs, preserve every per-case error, then run one fresh-process replay of the full case set.
3600-second producer and 3600-second replay caps; one thread; 8 GiB address-space limit; no retry or overwrite; write a new attempt path if interruption occurs.

invalidation_rules: Any matrix, embedding, cyclic-window, lower-projection or theorem-guard failure invalidates
Any replay mismatch invalidates; cap/error is not a degree
No timing, FFD/LFD or elite-base claim from these computations

decision_rule.text: Call a case exact_original_top only when its input/source/base hashes, theorem hypotheses, lower projection, overlap/kernel upper bound, and fresh-process replay all pass; otherwise retain error/incomplete and leave its degree unknown.
decision_rule.statistic: Per-case exact original-top degree or missing

graphs: Exact dreg by m, with one point per family/target case and the formula prediction shown; no uncertainty band because values are exact certificates, not sampled estimates.

inadmissible: Calling original-top regularity an FFD, LFD, affine solving degree, or full affine Hilbert function.
Calling the r=38 panel an elite-base ranking or training set; it contains one coordinate-bit base only.
Using prior-disjoint upper bounds, proxy labels, timeouts, or partial results as exact degrees.
Dropping failed inputs, changing m/family/target coverage, or reusing this output path for a retry.
Making an ECDLP recovery, speedup, or rho comparison from this exact algebraic computation.
